sections.heading: Decision brief: one offering from DSN, Starter Pack and the ASSA kit?
sections.text:
*Product scoping, 20 Oct 2026. For the 12 Nov decision session. This is a proposal, not a decision.*
Evidence labels used in this folder: O observed, D documented but unverified, I inferred, U unknown. Sources: evidence-index.md.

sections.heading: The answer in one paragraph
sections.text:
Yes, combine them, but at the level of one service and one client experience, not one codebase.

What we sell: we assess and organize a client's design system, in Figma and in code. They keep a control panel that lives inside their own repository (the "editable Storybook" Nuno and Rui described), plus the checks and AI files that keep the system organized after we leave.

What it is built from: the panel is assembled from what already exists:
- DSN's AI layer and repo editors;
- the Starter Pack's set-up wizard and Figma plugin;
- the ASSA kit's governance gates.

What it is not: a merge of their component libraries or token systems.

Two ways in:
- Start new (Path A): mostly built.
- Bring your system (Path B): our real differentiator, but unproven as a product. It goes into the MVP thin and service-led, behind a feasibility test.

sections.heading: Why (strongest reasons)
sections.text:
1. AI chat, theming and docs UIs are no longer a differentiator.
   - MCP read access is standard: Storybook MCP, zeroheight MCP, Knapsack MCP. Figma's own MCP writes to the canvas (Mar 2026). Supernova has agent writes in beta.
   - Theme configurators are crowded: shadcn/studio, tweakcn.
   - What competitors don't combine: a method for messy systems + edits that reach both code (as a reviewed PR) and Figma (as a 3-way-reviewed change set) + gates that block drift and AI invention, all running inside the client's repo. We have working pieces of each (O).
2. The pieces fit one journey; the codebases don't merge cheaply.

Project · Strongest in · Status

DSN · AI layer: 23-tool MCP, absences, 8 skills, audits; editors that open a PR · O
Starter Pack · Greenfield start: template, wizard, Figma 3-way review · O
ASSA kit · Governance: binding-parity gate, Figma-first source order, propose → confirm → apply · O

   The cost of merging them: three component implementations and three token grammars. DSN even bans the word "pressed" that the Starter Pack uses (O).
3. It matches what the board says we need.
   - The Audit lists "everyone builds a design system from scratch, on their own way" and "no decision map".
   - The DS Accelerator notes ask for "Figma link, Jira ticket or code repository → analyses → proposes solutions" and say "clients don't empathize seeing code on VSCode".
   - The control panel is that visual layer on real assets.
4. It keeps a settled decision intact: "the deliverable sold is the client-owned system, not the tool."
   - The panel ships *inside* the client's repo, so it becomes part of what they own.
   - This extends the decision; please confirm.
5. Our own three systems are the first test. If an adapter can't read our three grammars, it can't read a client's. That makes the feasibility test cheap and honest.

sections.heading: How it helps us sell
sections.text:
- Internally: one story and one 8-step demo (analysis §8) replace three separate tool demos. Colleagues learn "assess → organize → you keep the panel".
- Externally: the demo shows the client's problem first, then the before/after we did for a real client. It ends on what they keep. Every step is tagged *works today* or *proposed*, so we never demo a promise as a product.

sections.heading: MVP and service boundaries
sections.text:
In the MVP · Service (people) · Tool (client keeps)

Path A · Start new (DS Build) · Template + wizard (exist) → control panel on the same repo · Kick-off, brand decisions, adding the client's own components · Repo, Figma library, panel, CI checks, AI files
Path B · Bring your system (2-week audit → DS Accelerate / Scale) · Read-only assessment scan; one adapter profile (React + tokens in JSON or Figma variables); panel edits limited to tokens and component docs/metadata, as a PR · Assessment readout, naming/grammar decisions, adapter fixes, drift resolution, naming a governance owner, handover · Same as A, plus the assessment baseline
Out of MVP · Editing component code; non-React stacks; hosted multi-user editing; auto-merge; any "works with any design system" claim

Why both paths but unequal scope:
- Path A is our best demo and mostly exists.
- Path B is what makes us different, but no tool today reads a client system (O: the Starter Pack's "Mirror an existing Figma system" is marked *Coming later*). So Path B starts as service + a thin tool.

sections.heading: What each project keeps
sections.text:
- DSN: stays Nagarro's reference library and demo system. It supplies the AI layer and the editor code to start the panel from. Its separate brand configurator retires once the Starter Pack's is the single one.
- Starter Pack: stays the greenfield template, wizard and Figma plugin. It still needs a "save as a pull request" path. Remove the assa_abloy_test mode from its shared Figma file.
- ASSA kit: stays client work (Client IP, internal only). It is the proof that Path B works as a service, and the source of the governance gates (after removing the client brand).

sections.heading: Main trade-offs and uncertainties
sections.text:
- Brownfield adaptation is the risk. Tokens, Figma links and existing drift differ per client. We have one hand-made case (ASSA), not a tool. → The feasibility test decides whether Path B becomes product or stays service + scripts.
- No shared token grammar yet (D2). Deferring it avoids renaming 431 DSN and ~522 Starter Pack tokens and rebinding Figma files, but the adapter has to map between grammars.
- Repo writes are local-dev only in both DSN and the Starter Pack today (O). A hosted editor is out of scope; demos run locally or as read-only share links.
- Owner capacity: about 1 day/week each. A fourth product surface needs one named owner.
- Agent quality is untested end to end (O: unit tests only; DSN's editor AI is mocked).

sections.heading: Validation before investing
sections.text:
1. Stage 0: run one adapter against our own three systems (DSN, Starter Pack, ASSA tokens). Measure what maps without renaming.
2. Stage 1: one small public React design system with tokens in JSON and a public Figma file. Inspect, find drift, propose one edit, get a PR + Figma change set. Details: feasibility-experiment.md.
3. Demo test: run the 8-step demo with 3–5 colleagues (sales and delivery) and 1–2 friendly clients. Record whether they can retell the offer and what they'd buy.

sections.heading: Decisions needed from you
sections.text:
1. Direction: adopt "service + in-repo control panel; one experience, separate modules", or stay at Option 2 (shared contract only) for now?
2. Path B in the MVP: yes (thin, behind the test) or Path A only first?
3. Client keeps the panel: confirm this extends "we sell the client-owned system".
4. D2 token grammar: defer as proposed (the adapter maps between grammars)?
5. Panel owner: Rui (DSN site editors are closest) or Nuno (wizard, plugin, agent)? One owner, the other contributes.
6. Experiment system: pick from Workday Canvas Kit, GitHub Primer or Twilio Paste (each to verify), or propose one.
7. ASSA case clearance: can the before/after be shown externally, or anonymized only?
8. Board: is the earlier "Demo tools: product vision" (297:285, one engine / four modules) superseded by this? The old zones 4 (Merge or not) and 5 (Wireframes) are no longer on the page. Was that intentional?
9. Name (D7): "control panel" stays a working name until 12 Nov.

sections.heading: Market update (20 Oct, after the trend research)
sections.text:
Full radar and sources: market-trends.md.
- Direction unchanged; the case is stronger. Every AI tool now wants the system in its own format: Figma Specs and Make guidelines, Storybook MCP, Claude Design import, DESIGN.md, v0 registries, AGENTS.md/skills. Clients can't keep 8+ formats in sync, prove the output stays on-system, or govern agents that change the system. 61% of DS teams already lack people (zeroheight 2026, vendor survey).
- Two modules added:
  - a channel publisher (one contract → every agent format);
  - evals next to the CI checks.
- One spike added, outside the MVP: a generative-UI catalog (A2UI / MCP Apps allow-list).
- Eight service lines:
  1. AI-readiness clean-up + score
  2. One source, every channel
  3. Evals + CI gates
  4. Agent governance
  5. DTCG token architecture
  6. Generative UI catalog
  7. Toolchain + skills pack
  8. Enablement + ROI baseline
- Commodity, don't sell alone: installing an MCP, a theme configurator, a token CLI, a docs site, chat over docs, one DESIGN.md.
- Watch: Figma Specs/Agent and Claude Design import are moving into "manage the system with AI". Sell outcomes and governance, not the panel alone.
